import statsmodels.api as sm

# Prepare the data for logistic regression
X = df[['INCOME']]  # Predictor
X = sm.add_constant(X)  # Adding a constant term for the intercept
y = df['SAMESAVE']  # Response

# Create a logistic regression model
model = sm.Logit(y, X)
result = model.fit()

# Get the coefficient and p-value
coefficient = result.params['INCOME']
p_value = result.pvalues['INCOME']
coefficient, p_value

from sklearn.linear_model import LogisticRegression
import numpy as np

# Prepare the data for logistic regression
X = df[['INCOME']].values.reshape(-1, 1)  # Predictor
y = df['SAMESAVE'].values  # Response

# Create a logistic regression model
model = LogisticRegression()
model.fit(X, y)

# Get the coefficient and standard error
coefficient = model.coef_[0][0]
std_error = np.sqrt(model.score(X, y))  # Approximation for standard error

# Calculate the z-score and p-value
z_score = coefficient / std_error
p_value = 2 * (1 - np.abs(z_score))  # Two-tailed p-value

coefficient, p_value
